title: Layer Relativity for Excess Flood Limit Increases by Total Insured Value
content:
For an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** limit increase, the higher the layer sits, the lower the relativity applied to its rate.

**Rule.** The layer relativity applied to the layer rate for an increase is 80 percent where the dwelling limit on the latest declarations received for the underlying policy number on the policy record (or, where none are on file, the underlying dwelling limit on the policy record) plus the excess dwelling limit in force is at least 1500000, 90 percent where that sum is at least 750000 but below 1500000, and 100 percent otherwise.

The added limit is charged at the layer rate per 1,000 multiplied by this relativity. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

| Underlying dwelling limit plus excess dwelling limit in force (USD) | Layer relativity |
|---|---|
| 1500000 or more | 80 percent (0.8) |
| 750000 up to but not including 1500000 | 90 percent (0.9) |
| below 750000 | 100 percent |

**Boundaries (hypothetical).** An underlying dwelling limit of 250000 with 1250000 of excess in force sums to exactly 1500000 and takes 80 percent; with 1249999 it would take 90 percent. A sum of exactly 750000 takes 90 percent; 749999 takes 100 percent. Declarations received for a different underlying policy number are not read; where none for the policy's underlying number are on file, the underlying dwelling limit on the excess policy record is used.
